items.title: Example 3.62 · Rayleigh gradient and critical eigenvectors

source.anchor: Boumal2023 pre-publication annotations through2026-10-08, §3.8 Example3.62 and(3.40), printed44/PDF60; §3.4 Example3.36 printed36/PDF52; induced metric/gradient conventions §§3.7–3.8
source.attribution: Nicolas Boumal. ASTIS-authored restatement of the sphere application and its two stationarity directions; no source text/PDF redistributed.

items.statement: For a real symmetric matrix A, let F(x)=xᵀAx on the unit sphere with the metric induced by the Euclidean inner product. The chosen smooth ambient quadratic extension has gradient2Ax. The tangent projector sends u to u−⟨x,u⟩x, so the sphere gradient is2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x). Its vanishing is equivalent to Ax=⟨x,Ax⟩x; thus the stationary unit vectors are exactly eigenvectors of A, and every unit eigenvector is stationary.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, real symmetric matrix A and a unit vector x.
Unit sphere with the metric induced by the ambient inner product; F(x)=xᵀAx, the sphere restriction of the smooth quadratic extension.

formulae.label: Unit tangent projector and gradient
formulae.tex: P_xu=u-\langle x,u\rangle x,\qquad \operatorname{grad}_S F(x)=2(Ax-\langle x,Ax\rangle x).

formulae.label: Both directions of stationarity
formulae.tex: \operatorname{grad}_S F(x)=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x\ \Longleftrightarrow\ x\text{ is a unit eigenvector of }A.

obligations.label: Construct the actual restricted differential and its unique induced tangent representative, with explicit formula2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x).
Zero actual differential iff the Rayleigh-coefficient equation iff actual unit eigenvectorhood, including the converse.

bindings.boundary: Pointwise Example3.62 gradient formula and both critical/eigenvector conditions, using the genuine sphere differential and actual inclusion-induced pairing. Finite Euclidean symmetric matrices are represented coordinate-independently by continuous symmetric linear maps. No default chart-metric identification, global Riemannian bundle/gradient-field construction, extremal eigenvalue theorem, algorithm or convergence rate, arbitrary radius, general Prop3.61 or chapter completion.

assumption_deltas.source: Real symmetric matrix in a finite Euclidean space.
assumption_deltas.lean: FiniteDimensional real inner-product E and continuous-linear A with A.IsSymmetric; dim E=n+1.
assumption_deltas.reason: Coordinate-free representation in orthonormal coordinates; finite-dimensional continuity and sphere chart dimension are typing facts, not extra analytical restrictions.

assumption_deltas.source: Unit sphere with induced metric; smooth quadratic restriction.
assumption_deltas.lean: Literal restriction y↦⟨y,Ay⟩; actual mvfderiv paired through the actual inclusion derivative.
assumption_deltas.reason: The quadratic derivative is produced internally from symmetry; the induced pairing retains the source metric and actual tangent directions.

assumption_deltas.source: The induced sphere gradient is the tangent projection of the ambient quadratic gradient, with explicit formula2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x).
assumption_deltas.lean: Every ambient tangent candidate z represents the true restricted differential through the actual inclusion derivative iff z equals the explicit Rayleigh vector.
assumption_deltas.reason: The canonical parent proves the genuine restricted differential and unique induced tangent representative. Explicit unit projection gives this representative; no stationary/eigenvector conclusion is attributed to this declaration.
